With the **extra-note augmentation omitted**, the in-note beat model scores (Table 3, p. 5):
- **Precision:** 91.2
- **Recall:** 94.3
- **F-score:** 91.3

With **all augmentation methods**, the F-score is **92.2**, which is the best in that part of the table. Precision is 92.9 and recall is 93.7 (Table 3, p. 5).

**Possible extraction error:** The extra-note row is exactly the same as the "Use all features" row in the input-feature half of Table 3 (91.2 / 94.3 / 91.3, p. 5). That could be a real result or a copying error in the converted text, so check the PDF before quoting it.

On terminology, the data-augmentation section calls this method "Note introduction." It randomly adds notes that sound together with 0–100% of the existing notes, ±12 semitones away (p. 4). Table 3 calls it "Extra note" (p. 5).
